patch.value: Recovery bundle mines flag names from usage-error prose: scope errors like '--rebuild and --clear apply only to graph index' yield missing:--clear + suggested_retry appending the other invalid flag

Observed with pm graph analyze --rebuild (2026-07-20 manual E2E): the usage error '--rebuild and --clear apply only to graph index.' produces recovery.missing: --clear and suggested_retry: 'pm graph analyze --rebuild --clear' — the exact opposite of the fix. The recovery generator extracts flag tokens from arbitrary error MESSAGE prose and treats them as missing required flags. Sibling of the arity lineage (pm-6y58/pm-9qcr fixed arity, not provenance): flags named in a scope/mutual-exclusion explanation are not missing inputs. Fix direction: only derive missing-flag suggestions from structured metadata (contract-declared required flags), never from message text; scope/exclusivity usage errors should suggest removing the offending flag or switching subcommand.

Scope/mutual-exclusion usage errors produce no missing-flag rows and no suggested_retry that adds another invalid flag; missing-flag derivation consults only structured contract metadata; regression covers the graph --rebuild/--clear and --save-baseline scope errors

value.text: GitHub issue 757 is an instance of this class rather than a new defect. Same generator, same root cause: the recovery bundle derives flag suggestions from error-message prose instead of from the invoked command's declared flag contract. The new dimension it adds is cross-command leakage — --validate-close is a real pm flag, just not one pm update accepts — and a case where the correct recovery is a command redirect (use pm close) rather than any flag at all. Fixing this item must cover both: reject undeclared flags, and emit a command-level suggestion when no flag on the invoked command can resolve the failure. Sibling pm-ulqu stays separate: it is about rendering an enum flag's allowed values and about blocker ordering on a command that does accept the flag.

patch.value: Scope/mutual-exclusion usage errors produce no missing-flag rows and no suggested_retry that adds another invalid flag; missing-flag derivation consults only structured contract metadata; regression covers the graph --rebuild/--clear and --save-baseline scope errors; GH-757 instance is covered: under governance-preset strict a close attempted through pm update --status closed must not emit a suggested_retry that appends --validate-close, a flag pm update does not accept, because an agent following the bundle programmatically loops forever. Flag derivation consults only flags declared on the command actually invoked, and when no flag on that command can resolve the failure the bundle names the correct command instead
